topic: live Q&A (testing, activities, financial aid, ED/EA, undecided major)
speaker_role: panel of independent educational consultants (Lee Norwood of Annapolis College Consulting/College Sharks, plus co-hosts identified as Austin, Margaret, and Annie), on a CounselMore Software-hosted live stream, with a guest college advisor from Tulane calling in
commercial_incentive: yes - repeatedly directs viewers to pay for application reviews and counselor matching via support@councilmore.com and CounselMore's paid weighting-analysis service
key_insights: Panel advises that a focused set of 3-4 deeply-committed activities is generally viewed more favorably than 10 shallow/unrelated ones, especially for highly selective schools looking for depth over breadth

For AP vs. dual enrollment vs. IB, the consensus is 'it depends' on the student's school profile, goals, and test-taking strength, though one panelist favors AP generally since exam scores give colleges standardized proof of mastery

The single largest source of financial aid for most families is described as institutional merit/need-based aid from the college itself, more than chasing small outside scholarships, several of which (e.g., Rotary) can be 'backfilled' by the college reducing its own grant by the same amount

Applying 'undecided' is described as generally fine and even advantageous at some schools (e.g., cited exploratory programs at Purdue, Ithaca College, Roanoke College) since it avoids capped major-specific seat limits, but the application still needs 'congruence' - an internally consistent story - even if undecided

One panelist recounts a former Amherst College admissions case where a strong applicant was rejected because they wanted to study business, which the school didn't offer even via a local consortium arrangement

Regarding early decision risk, panelists share an anecdote of a student who got into Brown via ED but later wondered whether she could have gotten into a school she preferred, illustrating the tradeoff of committing early to a non-top-choice school
On dual enrollment specifically, panelists advise prioritizing courses not offered at the student's own high school (e.g., business, anthropology) rather than avoiding difficult in-house teachers
specific_numbers_or_facts: Cited example: University of Mississippi (Ole Miss) publishes a grid mapping GPA/test scores directly to merit scholarship amounts, per one panelist
Cited example: at some schools (e.g., UPenn per one panelist) roughly 50% of the incoming freshman class is filled through the early decision pool
A caller's SAT score of 1530 is characterized by a panelist as roughly the 98th percentile
notable_or_distinctive: Real-time, unscripted Q&A format surfaces specific institutional anecdotes (Amherst rejecting a strong applicant over an unavailable major, an AI-written viral rejection essay story, a swimmer's one-activity profile) that are more concrete than typical scripted advice videos.
reliability_notes: Live, multi-speaker auto-captioned stream with frequent cross-talk, interruptions, and some garbled/ambiguous phrasing (e.g., unclear question wording is occasionally misheard by panelists before being clarified); many claims are personal anecdotes or generalized practices from individual consultants rather than verified institutional policy, and the panel repeatedly steers viewers toward paid services.
